claims.text: Personal financial advisers ('relevant providers') are among the most regulated occupations in Australia: under the professional standards regime (Corporations Act 2001) they must meet an approved qualifications standard, pass the financial adviser exam, complete a professional year (new entrants), and undertake 40 hours/year CPD, governed by the Financial Planners and Advisers Code of Ethics 2019. Advisers must act in the client's best interest (Corporations Act s961B) and operate under an AFSL. The reforms raised the education bar, with all existing advisers required to meet the qualifications standard by 1 January 2026.

sources.title: Professional standards (financial advisers)
sources.whatItMeasured: ASIC professional-standards regime: qualifications, financial adviser exam, professional year, 40h CPD, Code of Ethics 2019; Best Interest Duty s961B.

claims.scope: Applies to personal advice to retail clients on relevant financial products; does not cover general advice or non-licensed guidance.

claims.text: Jobs and Skills Australia's Generative AI Capacity Study (August 2025) scores 358 ANZSCO occupations on task-level augmentability and automatability. It finds augmentation outweighs automation across the workforce: about 79% of Australian workers face low or very low automation risk, while routine clerical and administrative roles - including bookkeepers, receptionists, and business-analysis, sales, marketing and PR positions - carry the highest automation exposure. The study flags entry-level and clerical business roles as most exposed, with limited mobility options.

sources.title: Australia's AI Transition: Jobs, Skills and the Future of Work (Generative AI Capacity Study)
sources.whatItMeasured: JSA Gen AI Capacity Study, task-level ANZSCO v1.3 exposure, 358 occupations, Aug 2025.

claims.scope: Australian occupations nationally; model-derived task-level estimates. Adviser roles are professional, high-augmentation per JSA, with robo-advice as the automation edge.
claims.refuteNotes: Primary Australian government source; population = AU occupations; Aug 2025.
